basics.name: Chinese mechanism collections: HUANGYAN920/Mechanical ('MECH ENGINE' mechanism example library), Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology (XAUAT) 'Common typical mechanisms 3D library' (常见典型机构3D库), and Zhihu/CSDN mechanism GIF compilations (机械原理动图)
basics.url: HUANGYAN920/Mechanical: https://github.com/HUANGYAN920/Mechanical (README read via raw.githubusercontent.com; live demo https://huangyan920.github.io/Mechanical/) ; XAUAT 3D library: https://netedu.xauat.edu.cn/mcourse/10/jxsj/ziyuan/3d/shejiku.htm ; Zhihu GIF compilations: found in search results but not opened (zhihu.com and csdn.net are blocked from this environment) [uncertain]
basics.resource_type: Mixed: GitHub repo with an interactive tool (HUANGYAN920, a single-file HTML page of parametric kinematic simulations); digital library of 3D CAD models from a university course site (XAUAT, SolidWorks eDrawings files); informal GIF compilations on a Q&A/blog platform (Zhihu, CSDN)
basics.license: HUANGYAN920/Mechanical: MIT License ('Copyright (c) 2026 MECH ENGINE contributors'), so the code, the mechanism list and the drawings it generates can be reused, including commercially, with the copyright notice kept. XAUAT: no licence stated; it is a university course page, so treat it as all rights reserved and link only [uncertain]. Zhihu GIF compilations: usually reposted GIFs with no clear licence or original source; do not reuse [uncertain]
basics.language: Chinese (Simplified); HUANGYAN920 also gives an English code name for each mechanism (e.g. SLIDER-CRANK, GENEVA, HARMONIC-DRIVE)
basics.year: HUANGYAN920/Mechanical: 2026 (LICENSE copyright year); an earlier indexed description mentioned 100 mechanisms in 9 categories, while the current README (read September 2026) lists 257 in 11, so it is growing quickly [uncertain]. XAUAT: July 2010 (page metadata and a closing note '2010.7'); not updated since. Zhihu compilations: various posts, roughly 2020-2024 [uncertain]
basics.access_barrier: HUANGYAN920: none (open the web page or double-click the downloaded index.html; works offline). XAUAT: desktop install; each model page embeds a SolidWorks eDrawings ActiveX control that needs Internet Explorer 5.5+ or the eDrawings viewer (the page links an old 'eDrawingsForProE_32bit_7_1' installer), so the 3D animations will not open in modern browsers. Zhihu: free, but some content needs the Zhihu app or login to see fully [uncertain]
basics.image_license: HUANGYAN920: all drawings are SVG generated by the MIT-licensed code, so exported SVG/PNG images are reusable under MIT. XAUAT: student-made SolidWorks models and screenshots with no licence stated [uncertain]. Zhihu GIFs: mostly reposted from other creators (often uncredited), rights unclear [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: HUANGYAN920: community or unvetted (one GitHub author; not peer-reviewed; descriptions are short and unchecked). XAUAT: educator (an excerpt from an undergraduate research paper supervised by Associate Professor Tong Zhixue (同志学), compiled by Zhang Xizhong (张西仲), citing standard Chinese textbooks such as Sun Huan's Theory of Machines 7th ed.). Zhihu: community or unvetted

coverage.covers: HUANGYAN920/Mechanical: 257 mechanisms, each a live kinematic simulation with parameter sliders, in 11 categories: linkages 64, cams 25, gears 34, intermittent motion 22, screw mechanisms 19, clamping 22, hydraulics 20, universal/shaft couplings 17, flexible drives (belts, chains, ropes) 22, robot arms 6, bio-inspired 6. XAUAT: about 20 SolidWorks 3D models with motion simulation of application examples from a Theory of Machines course (dump truck lift, crank press, jaw crusher, twin-cylinder engine, aircraft landing gear, camera crane, front-wheel steering, scissor lift, single-cylinder engine valve train, punch-head cam control, fixed-axis and epicyclic gear trains, internal gears, Geneva wheel, incomplete gear and gear-rack, single and double universal joints, film projector feed, worktable cam-linkage, automatic loader, shaper), plus short theory on linkage, cam, gear and intermittent mechanism types. Zhihu GIF compilations: posts collecting 29-100 GIFs of gears, cams, linkages, clamping and feeding mechanisms (e.g. '100 mechanical GIFs', '80 mechanical principle GIFs'), not verified here [uncertain]
coverage.organisation: HUANGYAN920: category filter buttons, full-text search over Chinese name, category and English code name, pages of 12 cards, and a detail pop-up per mechanism. Works well for browsing by family but requires Chinese or the English code names; there is no 'what do you need' route. XAUAT: one long page following textbook chapters (linkages, cams, gears and gear trains, other common mechanisms, combined mechanisms, mechanisms in machines), each application with principle, 3D model link and simulation-result description. Zhihu: unordered lists of GIFs with one-line captions [uncertain]
coverage.scope_match: medium-high for HUANGYAN920: many in-scope mechanism and transmission TYPES, including unusual ones (harmonic drive, cycloidal drive, ball planetary reducer, magnetic gear, sprag and overrunning clutches, one-way bearing, ball detent, safety coupling, toggle clamp, differential screw, roller screw, Klann and Jansen linkages), but it is aimed at industrial machine design, not at connections, and has no snap fits, print-in-place, adhesives or powered latches except an electromagnetic chuck. Low for XAUAT (about 20 classic textbook examples, largely whole machines) and for the Zhihu compilations (unsourced GIFs)
coverage.taxonomy_used: HUANGYAN920: 11 top-level categories, a Chinese Theory of Machines scheme extended with applications: linkage mechanisms (连杆机构), cam mechanisms (凸轮机构), gear mechanisms (齿轮机构), intermittent-motion mechanisms (间歇机构), screw mechanisms (螺旋机构), clamping mechanisms (夹紧机构), hydraulic mechanisms (液压机构), universal/coupling transmissions (万向传动), flexible (belt/chain/rope) transmissions (挠性传动), robot mechanisms (机器人机构), bio-inspired mechanisms (仿生机构). XAUAT: textbook chapters (linkage, cam, gear/gear train, other common mechanisms incl. intermittent, combined mechanisms, mechanisms in machines), with cam sub-classification by cam shape, follower shape, follower motion and closure method (force-closed vs form-closed), and gear trains split into fixed-axis, epicyclic and compound
coverage.example_types: harmonic drive / strain-wave gear (谐波减速器), cycloidal pin-wheel reducer (摆线针轮减速), ball planetary reducer (钢球行星减速), few-tooth-difference planetary reducer (少齿差行星减速), magnetic gear (磁齿轮, slips when overloaded), non-circular (elliptical) gears, differential (差速器), overrunning clutch (超越离合器), sprag clutch / friction one-way clutch (摩擦式单向离合器), one-way bearing (单向轴承), reversible ratchet (双向棘轮), Geneva drive incl. star and twin-station versions (槽轮机构), escapement (擒纵机构), ball detent indexing (钢球定位), globoid indexing cam (弧面分度凸轮), safety coupling with shear pin or ball release (安全联轴器), Oldham coupling (十字滑块联轴器), toggle clamp / toggle press (肘杆), wedge clamp and wedge force booster (斜楔增力), eccentric cam clamp (偏心夹紧), expanding mandrel (涨瓣心轴), collet (弹性筒夹), differential screw (差动螺旋), planetary roller screw (行星滚柱丝杠), constant-breadth and constant-diameter cams, Jansen and Klann walking linkages, Peaucellier and Hart straight-line linkages
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering and machine design (industrial machinery, automation fixtures, vehicles); nothing specific to 3D printing, though the parametric simulations are useful for designing printed linkages and gears. XAUAT is SolidWorks CAD modelling and motion simulation
coverage.item_count: HUANGYAN920: 257 mechanisms (counted in index.html: 64 + 25 + 34 + 22 + 19 + 22 + 20 + 17 + 22 + 6 + 6). XAUAT: 24 linked model pages (about 20 distinct models, some linked twice). Zhihu compilations: individual posts of about 29-100 GIFs each [uncertain]
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: HUANGYAN920: one-way/ratchet yes (ratchet, double and reversible ratchet, internal ratchet, overrunning clutch, sprag clutch, one-way bearing); indexing/detent yes (Geneva variants, cam indexer, indexing plate, ball detent, worm indexing table, indexing cylinder); torque-limiting yes (safety coupling that shears or releases on overload; magnetic gear described as disconnecting on overload); over-centre yes as toggle clamp and toggle press (dead-centre force multiplication); self-locking only implied by screw jack, worm lift and wedge clamps [uncertain]; gear trains/gearboxes yes and strong (planetary, epicyclic, double planetary, harmonic, cycloidal, few-tooth-difference, ball planetary, multi-stage, differential, worm, hypoid, face and crown gears); compliant partly (diaphragm and bellows couplings, flexible soft gripper); powered connectors only as electromagnetic chuck (电磁吸盘), vacuum cup and pneumatic/hydraulic grippers; hand-release only, print-in-place and adhesives not covered. XAUAT: uses dead-point (over-centre) locking in the aircraft landing gear example; Geneva and incomplete-gear intermittent motion; epicyclic gear train. Zhihu: includes clamping mechanisms (e.g. non-self-locking push-pull clamping) per search snippets [uncertain]
coverage.entry_structure: HUANGYAN920: card with Chinese name, English code name, category and index number; detail pop-up with a large live SVG simulation, a one-sentence description (principle, features, typical use), a parameter quick-reference table (e.g. principle, function, reset method, typical application), sliders for geometry (crank radius, link length, tooth count, pivot positions), speed and zoom, a pausable timeline, presets for some mechanisms, export to SVG/PNG/parameter JSON and a shareable link. XAUAT: working principle paragraph, a link to the 3D eDrawings model with motion, and a description of the simulated velocity/displacement curves. Zhihu: GIF plus a caption
coverage.audience_level: HUANGYAN920: undergraduate and professional machine designers (useful to hobbyists who can read the English code names). XAUAT: undergraduate. Zhihu: hobbyist and general public

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium for HUANGYAN920: moving, adjustable pictures are very intuitive and each description is one short sentence, but everything is in Chinese with engineering terms, and the English is only an upper-case code name. Low for XAUAT (textbook Chinese, broken viewer). Medium for Zhihu GIFs (very visual but no explanation or naming consistency) [uncertain]
usefulness.has_images: yes: HUANGYAN920 draws clean schematic line drawings (SVG) in a 'tech HUD' style, exportable as SVG/PNG; XAUAT has one inline image on the main page and relies on the 3D model files; Zhihu posts are mostly GIFs [uncertain]
usefulness.has_animations: yes: HUANGYAN920 has 257 real-time kinematic simulations (solved from geometry each frame, not canned frames), all with parameter sliders, pause and timeline scrubbing; XAUAT has SolidWorks eDrawings 3D animations that need an obsolete ActiveX plug-in; Zhihu compilations are GIF animations [uncertain]
usefulness.gaps: All in Chinese; HUANGYAN920 has no plain-language explanation, no design rules, no real-world photos, no sources, and some simulations are schematic stand-ins (e.g. the safety coupling reuses a two-disc sketch); nothing on joints for 3D printing, snap fits, compliant hinges, adhesives or powered latches. XAUAT is small, dated 2010 and effectively unviewable. Zhihu GIFs are unsourced reposts, often watermarked, and not stable to link
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: HUANGYAN920: yes, partly. The page encodes the chosen mechanism and parameters in the URL hash ('#m=<key>&p=<parameters>') via its 'copy share link' button, so a per-mechanism link can be built from the key (e.g. key 'ball-detent'); the base URL is https://huangyan920.github.io/Mechanical/ . Such hash links were not tested here [uncertain]. XAUAT: per-model pages exist (e.g. https://netedu.xauat.edu.cn/mcourse/10/jxsj/ziyuan/3d/caolun.htm for the Geneva wheel) but need eDrawings, so not useful. Zhihu: not recommended
usefulness.reusable_data: HUANGYAN920: highly reusable. The whole library is one MECHANISMS JavaScript object in index.html, with a key, Chinese name, English code, category, index number, description, parameter table, slider definitions and a build() drawing function per mechanism; MIT licence allows reuse of the list, text and code with attribution. XAUAT: scrape-only list, no licence. Zhihu: not reusable
usefulness.maintained: HUANGYAN920: active in 2026 (README says 257 mechanisms, all parametric; demo online and identical to index.html). XAUAT: online but frozen since July 2010, and its parent course directory returns 403/404. Zhihu: posts online but not maintained collections; could not be opened from this environment
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Live, parameter-driven simulations instead of GIFs: let the reader drag link lengths or tooth counts and see the motion change. (2) A pausable timeline to freeze and explain a moment. (3) One data object per mechanism (name, English name, category, one-line description, key facts table, sliders) driving the whole site, as a lightweight catalogue format. (4) A 'key facts' table per entry with rows such as principle, function, reset method (e.g. 'replace part' for a shear-pin coupling) and typical application; the reset row maps well onto the project's reuse and removability filters. (5) Share links that encode the mechanism and settings. (6) Export an SVG/PNG of the current pose for use in entries (MIT licensed). (7) XAUAT's habit of teaching each type through a real application (landing gear = dead-point lock, projector = Geneva) helps beginners
usefulness.design_rules_given: Few: HUANGYAN920 gives qualitative parameter tables (e.g. repeatability 'good', feel 'clear' for the ball detent) and simulation ratios, not numeric design rules. XAUAT gives simulated speeds and ratio checks for its examples and the conditions for constant-velocity double universal joints. No clearances, fits or torque values
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Yes (HUANGYAN920): every one of the 257 mechanisms is parametric in the browser (sliders for geometry, speed and zoom, presets such as offset quick-return or double crank) and can export SVG, PNG and parameter JSON. It is a 2D kinematic drawing tool, not a CAD/STL generator. XAUAT and Zhihu: no
usefulness.file_formats: HUANGYAN920: single HTML file with inline SVG and JavaScript; exports SVG, PNG and JSON. XAUAT: HTML pages embedding SolidWorks eDrawings data (and a RAR viewer installer). Zhihu/CSDN: GIF, sometimes Flash or video [uncertain]
usefulness.terminology_value: high for Chinese names: HUANGYAN920 pairs standard Chinese mechanism names with English code names for 257 types (e.g. 槽轮机构 = Geneva, 超越离合器 = overrunning clutch, 谐波减速器 = harmonic drive, 钢球定位 = ball detent, 肘杆 = toggle), useful for adding Chinese aliases; check the English codes against a proper glossary since some are abbreviations
usefulness.decision_support: None: HUANGYAN920 has category filters, text search and hit counts but no selector, flow chart or comparison tables; XAUAT and Zhihu have none
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: HUANGYAN920's list follows the standard Chinese Theory of Machines textbook scheme plus a common set of industrial examples; it overlaps Nguyen Duc Thang's animated mechanisms, DMG-Lib and Wikipedia for the classic linkages, cams and gears; drawings are its own code. The repo's GitHub description (seen only in search results) repeats a stock Chinese phrase used by GIF compilations ('用一种简短的动画方式清晰的表达出了机械运动过程...'), suggesting an earlier GIF/video focus [uncertain]. XAUAT is based on Sun Huan et al., Theory of Machines 7th ed. (2006) and other cited Chinese textbooks. Zhihu GIF compilations largely repost GIFs from Nguyen Duc Thang, 507 Mechanical Movements-style animations and Chinese WeChat accounts [uncertain]
